extracted.intended_audience: small-press editors, literary magazine editors, and short-story writers seeking Pushcart recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural rules used to select short fiction for the Pushcart Prize: what kinds of stories are eligible, what qualities are favored, and how nominations and judging are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: source publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawn exclusively from independent publications (small presses & lit mags).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Prize honors stories published in independent/small-press venues; nominations come from editors of small presses and literary magazines as well as Pushcart's Contributing Editors. This implies works originally published by major commercial publishers are outside the intended pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual selection quota
rubrics_metrics.description: ~20 short stories per year are selected for the Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughly twenty stories are chosen annually, so selection is highly competitive and limited in number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original prose narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original prose narratives that showcase exceptional craft" — the Prize emphasizes original short fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be original prose narratives (i.e., short stories rather than other forms) and must demonstrate notable craft; originality in voice, language, or approach is implied by the wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for standalone short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Standalone short stories preferred over novel excerpts; highlights "self-contained artistry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Prize favors stories that read as complete, self-contained works rather than portions of longer works. This favors narratives with a sense of completion and independent artistic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Average length ~5,000 words — favoring complete narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a guidance rather than a strict rule: the Prize historically favors stories around 5,000 words that allow for a fully developed short-story arc, but atypical lengths may still be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional craft at sentence and structural level
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on "exceptional craft" both at the sentence level and in overall structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for finely crafted prose, precise sentence-level work, and strong structural choices (narrative architecture, pacing, form) that together demonstrate high literary skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight into human experience / substantive vision
rubrics_metrics.description: "Insight into human experience" — fiction with substantive moral/psychological vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond craft, selected stories typically offer meaningful insight into characters, relationships, or human conditions — an intellectual or emotional depth that conveys a moral, psychological, or existential perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic and topical tendencies often favored
rubrics_metrics.description: Often: literary realism, formally daring work, marginalized voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not mandatory, the Prize frequently recognizes works in literary realism and also rewards formal daring and the amplification of marginalized voices. These tendencies describe patterns of past selections rather than hard requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination limits and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors of small presses may nominate up to 6 works; Pushcart's Contributing Editors also nominate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a cap on nominations from individual small-press editors (up to six), and Contributing Editors have their own nominating role. Compliance with nomination limits and proper nomination channels is part of the procedural eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection panel and anonymity practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Final selections are made by a panel of past winners and editors; judges' identities are withheld to preserve integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is done by an appointed panel composed of past winners and editors. Judges' identities being withheld indicates a deliberate procedural choice to protect impartiality and the integrity of the selection process.
